events.title: From Frightful to Delightful: East Asian Monsters in the Stacks
events.summary: Celebrate Halloween in the Asia Library, and meet the monsters lurking in our collections! This exhibit brings together demons, shape-shifters, and mythical beasts from across East Asia. You'll discover how those East Asian monstrous creatures have frightened, amused, and fascinated audiences across cultures and generations. Come encounter whimsical and eerie beings that defy easy categorization, and discover what they can tell us about the societies that created and reimagined them. This event offers a playful exploration of East Asian folklore, literature, art, and popular culture. Costumes and curiosity are welcome! Third Thursdays at the Library is a themed monthly open house where we share materials from our collections. While you’re here, pick up a passport and collect a stamp from each of this month's Third Thursday locations — Asia Library, Clark Library, International Studies, and the Special Collections Research Center — to win a prize!

events.title: UMS presents Sphinx Virtuosi with J'Nai Bridges, mezzo-soprano
events.summary: PROGRAM Rachel McFarlane American Dialogue Roberto Sierra Sinfonietta for Strings Damien Geter Declaration Jessie Montgomery Banner Maurice Ravel“Blues” from Violin Sonata (arr. Mladen Miloradovic) Igor Stravinsky Concerto in D for string orchestra (“Basle”) The Sphinx Virtuosi celebrate our country’s ever-evolving story through newly commissioned works and reimagined classics that give voice to our shared ideals and diverse perspectives. The program includes Rachel McFarlane’s American Dialogue, as well as the timeless “Blues” movement from Maurice Ravel’s Violin Sonata. Works by Roberto Sierra and Jessie Montgomery offer vibrant explorations of heritage and transformation, while Stravinsky’s Concerto for Strings in D connects past and present in a timeless meditation on artistic freedom. Through music that bridges time and culture, this program invites audiences to engage in a musical conversation about who we are — and who we aspire to become. American mezzo-soprano J’Nai Bridges, lauded by The New York Times for her “plush-voiced mezzo-soprano,” joins the Sphinx Virtuosi for a bold, new song cycle by Damien Geter with a libretto by Aaron Dworkin.

events.title: Grand Vision
events.summary: Visiting artist Olayami Dabls is a storyteller, curator, educator, and mentor. He is the founder of the MBAD African Bead Museum in Detroit. Through material culture, Dabls presents commentary on the past, present, and future from African and African-American perspectives, with the understanding that generations of African ancestors used visual materials to convey information about their identity as well as send messages for healing and protection. Dabls is a luminary; for decades he has re-imagined what a museum space can be, accessible to everyone, free from the underpinnings of colonialism and the Western, often white, frame. *Grand Vision* includes a conceptual installation in the Gallery, presenting Dabls’s own work in visual conversation with African beads and artifacts from Dabls’s Bead Museum collections. Additionally, Dabls’s iconic outdoor sculpture *Iron Teaching Rocks Table Manners* will be installed on the U-M campus grounds near UMMA, at the intersection of State Street and South University from September 17- October 11, 2026. The project’s range intends to more fully articulate the many facets of Dabls’ creative practice, and the overlay of art, history, identity, community, and healing.

events.title: Best of FAMU
events.summary: The program of short films offers a representative cross-section of works created at Prague’s film school throughout its eighty-year history. The eight selected films vividly illustrate the diversity of student filmmaking, encompassing fiction, documentary, and animation, as well as both lesser-known works and internationally acclaimed titles (including a Student Academy Award winner). Together, they span a wide range of styles and genres, from pantomime slapstick and historical drama to mockumentary and animated fantasy. The selection includes early works by filmmakers such as Jan Němec and Jan Svěrák, who went on to become major figures in Czech cinema, alongside outstanding talents from younger generations, including Daria Kashcheeva, Bára Anna Stejskalová, and Marie-Magdalena Kochová. List of films: • Encounter • The Loaf of Bread • Oil Gobblers • Closed Due to the Family Mourning • Pripyat Piano • Daughter • Love Is Just a Death Away • 3 MWh Film Synopsis: • Encounter (Vladimír Svitáček, 1953, 5 min.) Vladimír Svitáček, later renowned as a co-creator of the multimedia theatre Laterna Magika and the world’s first interactive movie Kinoautomat, depicts a crowded Prague tram in this pantomime-inspired comic sketch, featuring outstanding performances by the young Miloš Kopecký and Jiří Sovák. The film also includes rare archival footage of the area surrounding Prague’s Main Railway Station. Director: Vladimír Svitáček Screenwriter: Vladimír Svitáček Director of Photography: Jerzy Kotowski Original Score: Jaroslav Ježek Cast: Miloš Kopecký, Jiří Sovák, Jana Werichová-Kvapilová, Káťa Kopecká etc. • The Loaf of Bread (Jan Němec, 1960, 11 min.) This early student film by Jan Němec, one of the leading figures of the Czech New Wave, can be regarded as a thematic precursor to his masterpiece Diamonds of the Night. In the final days of the Second World War, a train carrying concentration camp prisoners stands at a railway station. Three exhausted inmates contemplate how to reach a nearby freight car loaded with bread, hoping to regain enough strength before attempting their escape. Director: Jan Němec Screenwriter: Jan Němec, Eva Límanová Director of Photography: Jiří Šámal Cast: Ivan Renč, Jan Bartůšek, Oldřich Bláha • Oil Gobblers (Jan Svěrák, 1988, 20 min.) Jan Svěrák’s Oil Gobblers was made in 1988 as his graduation film at the Department of Documentary Film. This mockumentary follows a fictional scientific expedition in search of an unknown creature known as the “oil gobbler,” whose very existence defies all the principles of life in a healthy natural environment. The film turns a serious ecological issue completely on its head, presenting its story with such convincing realism that the hoax is almost flawless. In June 1989, the film received the Student Academy Award presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. Director, Screenwriter: Jan Svěrák Director of Photography: Ladislav Štěpán Original Score: Vendula Kašpárková Cast: Lubomír Beneš, Jiří Němec, Ivo Kašpar, Jan Rokyta, Emil Nedbal etc. • Closed Due to the Family Mourning (Saša Gedeon, 1991, 9 min.) This short film by screenwriter and director Saša Gedeon is based on Alberto Moravia’s short story Fire. A bittersweet vignette, it portrays a single day in a small Italian barbershop on the eve of the Second World War. Rather than relying on an intricate plot, the film derives its power from its understated emotional tension and evocative atmosphere. Made during Gedeon’s second year at FAMU, the film received an award at the FFICS – International Festival of Film School Students in Tokyo in 1992. The prize money enabled the director to make his feature-film debut Indian Summer. Director, Screenwriter: Saša Gedeon Director of Photography: Miloš Kabyl Cast: Barbora Hrzánová, David Vávra, Jakub Špalek, Renata Beccerová • Pripyat Piano (Eliška Cílková, 2019, 18 min.) Many of the original inhabitants of Pripyat have never come to terms with the Chernobyl disaster. Some of them began composing their own songs and poems and returning to their apartments within the forbidden radioactive zone. This documentary concert, reflecting on the presence of a unique space, calls for the return of humankind as both creator and performer. In the poems and songs recited by the former residents of Pripyat themselves, a powerful connection between people and home can still be heard to endure. The film has been screened at major documentary film festivals and has received numerous awards. Director, Editor, Original Score, Sound Design: Eliška Cílková Director of Photography: Tomáš Frkal • Daughter (Daria Kashcheeva, 2019, 14 min.) This puppet animation by Daria Kashcheeva tells the story of a father and daughter who, despite mutual misunderstanding, eventually find their way back to each other. The film’s emotional intensity and unsettling atmosphere are enhanced by an unusually dynamic camera – rare in animation – and by close-up shots of the puppets’ faces, whose expressions feel remarkably lifelike. The film won the prestigious Student Academy Award (in the category of international animation) and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film. Director, Screenwriter, Director of Photography: Daria Kashcheeva Original Score: Petr Vrba Editor: Alexander Kashcheev • Love Is Just a Death Away (Bára Anna Stejskalová, 2020, 10 min.) A dead dog, a landfill, and beautiful moths high in the sky – this is the world of Steve, a parasite desperately searching for a kindred soul. Yet every attempt at connection ends in disappointment. A small bird he saves from another dog dies. A rat that touches him dies. Cockroaches, under the guise of friendship, strip him down to the bone. Completely defenseless inside the skeleton of his former host, he nearly loses his life under the wheels of a machine that crushes waste. The film has screened at numerous festivals and received the award for Best Student Animated Short Film as well as the Audience Award for Best Animated Short Film at the Palm Springs International Film Festival. Director, Editor, Original Score, Sound Design: Bára Anna Stejskalová Director of Photography: Tomáš Frkal • 3 MWh (Marie-Magdalena Kochová, 2024, 13 min.) An employee at a nuclear power plant, obsessed with counting, sets himself a limit on how much electricity he wants to consume for the rest of his life. In this dark yet masterful cinematic poem shot on 35mm film, Marie-Magdalena Kochová presents the story of a man whose life is moving toward transformation. It is a tender acceptance of the idea that we are not only our bodies, but also energy. The film has been screened at numerous international festivals and Czech Film Critics Award. Director: Marie-Magdalena Kochová Screenwriter: Josef Kokta Director of Photography: Kristina Kůlová Original Score: Haštal Hapka Cast: Jaroslav Pížl

events.title: Comics Beyond Sight
events.summary: This exhibit covers a variety of creative approaches to comics visual accessibility, and by extension visual accessibility broadly. Those approaches range from multimedia (audio and textual descriptions) through multidimensional and emerging technologies strategies (3D printing, haptics, and screen-based mobile touch interfaces). It demonstrates that comics can be made accessible. Learn about the international efforts of innovators in the realm of comics accessibility for those who are blind or have low vision, assembled by the Accessible Comics Collective at San Francisco State University (SFSU) with the expertise of blind access professionals. Emily Beitiks was the accessibility lead for the content creation of the exhibit. She is the co-director for the San Francisco Disability Cultural Center (the first civically funded disability culture center on the planet!), and prior to that, the director of the Longmore Institute on Disability. Nick Sousanis (SFSU), the lead creative organizer of the exhibit, is a Detroit native and was the first person to draw his dissertation in comics format, subsequently published as the graphic novel Unflattening. View the exhibit anytime the Hatcher Library is open, and join us for an opening presentation on Friday, October 2nd, 1:00pm - 4:00pm.

events.title: THEATRE l My Daddy is Haunted!
events.summary: My Daddy is Haunted! Comedy/Horror One Act - No intermission Running time Approx 70 minutes Join us at the Ant Hall this October for the debut of Planet Ant's original horror comedy, My Daddy is Haunted! A long time ago, in a small eastern European town , Sterling Mandrake (a really evil warlock), was accused of heresy and burned alive by a righteous nun trying to save the village. For 164 years his castle lay dormant, perched upon a crumbling mountain. That is until the Maplesquatch family arrives for a vacation they’ll never forget! Father Orwin, (A dorky but loving father) surprises his wife Margo (A bestselling romance author), Teenage daughter Leona (She’s going through a phase right now), and son Linus (a 10 year old yo-yo master) with a trip to an ancient castle for some family fun. But the fun soon turns to terror as something starts to happen to dear old dad. Is that creepy painting alive? What’s with all the bugs? Is their daddy haunted? Come find out for yourself. If you dare! Hammer Horror meets National Lampoons Vacation! Where: Ant Hall Dates: October 9-24 with a special Halloween show October 31st! Time: Fridays & Saturdays at 8pm l Sundays 3pm Price: $30 online l $35 at the door Cast: Philip Digby Alexandra Van Ryn Freda Monroe Amanda Gonzalez Santí Barker Jaimee Giammanco Patrick Coppola Glen Midkiff August Dorien Elizabeth Magańa Crew: Written & Directed by Scott Sanford Assistant Directors- Jen Lee & Dylan Mirisola Executive Producer - Lauren Bickers Stage Manager- Jake De Leeuw Art & Visual Effects- Graham Hollister Set Design- Leslie Wacker Music- Phil Digby & Scott Sanford Poster- Li Miller

events.title: THEATRE l I'd Love to Have You for Dinner
events.venue: Black Box - 2357 Caniff Hamtramck, MI 48212 - Entrance in the rear
events.summary: I'd Love to Have You For Dinner Psychological Thriller 2 Acts w/ Intermission 1 Hour 40 Minutes IMPORTANT NOTE: This show contains extreme violence and gore. Viewer discretion is advised. Two lovebirds, Ania and Charles, meet for their first-and-three-quarters date: a home cooked meal. But there is a secret at the table: one of them eats people. The other, of course, is fully aware, because the one who eats people – Ania – is an ancient vampire, while the other – Charles – hunts and eats vampires alive. When these forces – life, and unlife – go for each other’s throats, who will go home with a full stomach? This two act, four-course horror/thriller highlights legacy, cannibalism, the inevitability of personal failure, and the complex moral nature of predation in all its incarnations. Starring: Celah Convis as Ania Komorowski Alex Aho as Charles Marlene Goss as Lady Michele Harte, Director and Writer Julia Lebrell, Stage Manager Max Wray, Marketing

events.title: Faster and More Fun: American Home Cooking in the 1920s
events.summary: Visit the Hatcher Gallery Exhibit Room to see historical materials that illustrate women’s changing relationship with food, cooking, and technology during the heady decade of the 1920s, sandwiched between WWI and the Great Depression. This exhibit features materials from the Janice Bluestein Longone Culinary Archive, as well as select items from the Art, Architecture, and Engineering Special Collections and the Transportation History Collection. As America rang in a new decade in the 1920s, cookbook authors and appliance manufacturers stood ready to offer the newly emancipated and forward-thinking American woman a vision for her future, a vision that would be scientifically grounded, speedy enough to make time for leisure as well as housework, and guaranteed to bring fun to that most humdrum of chores: planning and preparing meals for a family three times a day, 365 days a year.
